outcome.spec:
Audit pull request https://github.com/RankOneLabs/oakridge/pull/790 (branch cohort/configured-question-evidence/79693b) in repository oakridge. This is an isolated verification run of the committed development definition, not feature work: its only purpose is real plan, brief, build_result and assessment artifacts for observation to capture. Produce exactly one cohort, named audit, with two tasks. T1: observation/graders.json is the only grader selection, and startup validates and registers it (observation/src/grading/configuration.ts, observation/src/main.ts). T2: cited files are read at the assessed commit, and a file missing there is recorded as absent (observation/src/producers/oakridge/evidence.ts, observation/src/storage/git-repository-reader.ts).
The builder must not edit files, create commits, push, open or update any pull request, merge, reset a database or deploy. It inspects the checked-out branch, runs bun install if needed and then bun run --filter observation test once, and publishes build_result with the commit it inspected as head_sha and the actual test counts and output. A test that cannot run is a known issue, never a reason to invent results. It then publishes the existing pull request https://github.com/RankOneLabs/oakridge/pull/790 as the pr artifact, with branch cohort/configured-question-evidence/79693b.
The assessor assesses that same commit without changing anything. Give at least one finding per task. Every finding cites at least one file as path:start-end at that commit, for example observation/src/main.ts:20-40, and cites test output separately as test or output evidence. Report the builder's test run as test_evidence.
Keep the analysis, spec, tasks, plan and brief short; there are no ambiguous requirements to resolve.

Execution mode and lifecycle: Before proceeding past analysis, the operator must choose and record exactly one of: (A) authorize an audit-specific override that skips builder commit, push, and PR creation; publishes existing PR 790; skips assessor draft-state mutation; and stops after assessment capture with the workflow intentionally incomplete; (B) authorize feature work to add a non-mutating audit path to the committed workflow definition, then start a new verification run; or (C) permit the normal development builder, assessor, cohort-completion, and integration PR lifecycle and remove the immutability constraints.

body.summary: The audited branch and PR both point to commit 07eb9ab191d74f7aba6775d50a7bd81b13d5be1e. The repository already contains direct implementation and test evidence for T1 and T2, and the artifact schemas can represent the requested build and assessment evidence. The run is not executable as a strictly immutable audit under the committed development definition without an operator decision, because its builder, assessor, cohort completion, and integration contracts require pull-request or repository lifecycle actions that the specification forbids.

findings.description: The immutable audit contract conflicts with the committed development worker contract. workflow-config/prompts/development/build.md:21-42 requires commits, a push, a newly opened draft PR, and a PR artifact sourced from open_pr, while the specification forbids those actions and requires existing PR 790. workflow-config/prompts/development/assess.md:43-48 requires changing PR draft state; PR 790 is currently OPEN and draft, so a passing assessment would mark it ready. workflow-config/development.yaml:395-425 then requires PR completion and schedules an integration worker, whose workflow-config/prompts/development/integrate.md:1-1 requires commit, push, and another PR. The operator must choose among: (A) authorize an audit-specific override that skips builder commit/push/open, skips assessor draft mutation, publishes PR 790, and stops after assessment capture with the run intentionally incomplete; (B) authorize feature work to add an immutable audit path to the committed workflow, then rerun; or (C) relax the no-mutation requirement and accept the ordinary development PR/integration lifecycle. A performs the requested observation but cannot complete the current workflow, B changes the definition being verified, and C violates the stated isolation constraint.

T1 is concretely assessable at the audited commit. observation/src/grading/configuration.ts:17-54 defines and strictly parses graders.json as the selection source; observation/src/grading/configuration.ts:123-148 maps it to registered evaluators and capture pins; observation/src/main.ts:17-33 reads the configured selection through preparation; and observation/src/main.ts:65-85 validates credentials and registers definitions before serving. observation/tests/grader-configuration.test.ts directly covers selection uniqueness, validation, and startup preparation.

T2 is concretely assessable at the audited commit. observation/src/producers/oakridge/evidence.ts:81-101 obtains assessment head_sha, finds the repository holding that commit, reads each cited path with that commit, and emits is_absent:true/content:null for an absent file. observation/src/storage/git-repository-reader.ts:22-42 uses git cat-file against the exact commit and distinguishes absent from unavailable. observation/tests/producer-evidence.test.ts and observation/tests/git-repository-reader.test.ts directly cover exact-commit reads and missing-file evidence.

The requested evidence shape is supported: workflow-config/development.yaml defines build_result head_sha plus integer passed/failed/output test evidence and assessment findings with file, test, or output references; the assessor prompt requires assessment.head_sha to equal build_result.head_sha and requires evidence on every finding (workflow-config/prompts/development/assess.md:50-74). No observation test command was run during analysis, preserving the specification’s single builder test run.

requirements.description: Execute an isolated, immutable audit using the committed development definition and produce only the intended observation artifacts.
Create exactly one cohort named audit with tasks T1 and T2 and keep analysis, tasks, plan, and brief short.
Assess T1: graders.json is the only grader selection and startup validates and registers it.
Assess T2: file citations are read at assessment head_sha and absent files are retained as explicit absence evidence.
Have the builder make no repository or PR changes, run bun run --filter observation test exactly once, report actual results and inspected head_sha, and publish existing PR 790.
Have the assessor review the same commit without changing state, provide at least one file-cited finding per task with separate test/output evidence, and report build test results as test_evidence.

The alternatives have materially different repository, PR, and run-completion consequences and require operator selection.
